evaluated.why: Real jar downloaded and inspected for darwin-arm64v8 17.10.0 (embedded-postgres-binaries-darwin-arm64v8-17.10.0.jar, sha256 b8c73288326af937b632208110b1d629c404ebef7519f8bcc7fd72404c68a36a) — contains only postgres/initdb/pg_ctl. NO psql, pg_isready, pg_controldata, pg_dumpall, pg_restore, pg_upgrade. Zonky's own use case (JDBC-driven Java tests) never needs client tools, so they are not built. This repo's verify step forbids a `pg` driver outside packages/db (CLAUDE.md invariant 4), so health polling and dump/restore MUST shell out to real client binaries — zonky's set is structurally insufficient, not just inconvenient.

Confirmed reachable (HTTP 200) and downloaded postgresql-17.10-1-osx-binaries.zip in full: 358,193,796 bytes. This is the full EDB One-Click payload (pgAdmin4, StackBuilder, docs, etc.), not a minimal binaries-only bundle — 28x the size actually needed, mixed licensing (pgAdmin GPL + EDB StackBuilder terms bundled alongside core PG), and no generic tarball at all for Linux (the linux '-binaries.tar.gz' URL pattern 403'd; EDB's Linux path is apt/yum-repo only). Wrong shape for a T0-budget (docs/PLAN.md §9.2, idle RSS <=500MB) embedded install.

postgresql.org ships source tarballs and distro-specific packages (apt/yum/Homebrew), not portable pre-built binaries for all five target platforms from one source — would require building PG from source per-platform in CI, which is a materially bigger lift than fetching a pinned prebuilt artifact and contradicts P4.2's 'per-platform pinned binaries' framing (implies fetch-not-build).

Real end-to-end verification performed on this host (darwin-arm64, real network): downloaded postgresql-17.10.0-aarch64-apple-darwin.tar.gz (12,711,817 bytes), independently sha256'd (e15b5d3b86363d51fe06c9f26ee1d35d09b13951be82641b8f4b2d0e06e2c51e), matched the release's own published .sha256 sidecar AND GitHub's server-computed asset digest — three independent confirmations of the same bytes. Archive contains the FULL client toolset (postgres, initdb, pg_ctl, psql, pg_dump, pg_dumpall, pg_isready, pg_controldata, pg_restore, pg_upgrade, pg_basebackup, ...) under bin/, plus lib/share/include. Verified live: initdb (scram-sha-256, en_US.UTF-8, UTF8), postmaster start on both a unix socket AND TCP loopback (listen_addresses restricted), pg_isready, psql connect+query, pg_ctl status/stop, pg_dumpall -> fresh initdb -> psql restore round-trip with real row-count verification (500 rows), and pg_controldata's real output on two induced corruption modes (truncated pg_control -> short-read error; bit-flipped pg_control -> 'Calculated CRC checksum does not match' warning, exit 0) — see packages/provisioning-pg/src/corruption.ts for how these exact text signatures are classified. Small (11-51 MB per platform archive), covers all five installer-lane targets 1:1 via Rust target triples, PostgreSQL-License core (permissive, AGPL-3.0-compatible) plus theseus-rs's own ISC-equivalent wrapper LICENSE for the build/release tooling. Actively maintained (release cadence tracks upstream PG minors; 18.4.0 already published ahead of our 17.x pin, 16.x still published for the upgrade-test pin below).

sourcing.licenseNote: Two license layers, both permissive and AGPL-3.0-compatible in spirit: (1) the PostgreSQL binaries themselves are covered by the PostgreSQL License (MIT/BSD-style, https://opensource.org/licenses/postgresql) per each archive's bundled LICENSE/COPYRIGHT files, confirmed by direct inspection of the extracted darwin-arm64 17.10.0 and 16.14.0 archives; (2) theseus-rs's own packaging/build scripts carry an ISC-equivalent permissive license (bundled LICENSE file, 'Copyright (c) 2024, Theseus ... Permission to use, copy, modify, and distribute ...'). NEITHER is 'PostgreSQL License' or this exact ISC wording on LICENSE-INTENT.md's literal allow-list string set (MIT/ISC/BSD-2/BSD-3/Apache-2.0/AGPL-3.0/GPL-3.0/LGPL-3.0/MPL-2.0/0BSD/BlueOak-1.0.0/CC0-1.0/CC-BY-4.0/Unlicense/Python-2.0/WTFPL) because that allow-list is enforced by `license-checker` over npm package.json metadata, and these are fetched binaries (script + child_process/fs only, per this lane's LOCKFILE FROZEN constraint), never an npm dependency — license-checker never sees them, same structural gap ffmpeg-manifest.json's provenance block already flagged for lane I1's ffmpeg vendoring. DISCOVERY for the owner / lane W3 (AGPL readiness report): LICENSE-INTENT.md needs a 'Vendored non-npm binaries' section (ffmpeg from I1 + these PostgreSQL binaries) recording both are permissively licensed by manual inspection, not CI-scanned. Not edited here — out of this lane's ownership.

notes.archiveLayout: Every archive (tar.gz and zip alike) extracts to a single top-level directory named exactly `archiveTopDir` above, containing bin/ lib/ share/ include/ LICENSE COPYRIGHT README.md — verified identically across the darwin-arm64 tar.gz and the windows-x64 zip (full listing inspected). scripts/fetch-embedded-pg.mjs's extraction step strips this top directory so the vendor dir always ends up as `<vendorDir>/<platform>/<version>/{bin,lib,share,include}` regardless of source archive naming.
notes.linuxGlibcBaseline: linux-x64/linux-arm64 above are the 'gnu' (glibc-linked) target triples — the right default for desktop/server distros (installer lanes I1/I2's target). theseus-rs also publishes 'musl' variants (x86_64-unknown-linux-musl, aarch64-unknown-linux-musl) for Alpine-style bases; not pinned here since neither I1 (tarball+systemd) nor I2 (Docker, own Dockerfile/base-image choice) asked for musl in their dispatch — DISCOVERY for I2 if the production Docker image ever moves to an Alpine base.
notes.windowsArchiveChoice: theseus-rs publishes BOTH .tar.gz and .zip for windows-x64; .zip pinned here as the more Windows-native format (no tar/gzip dependency assumption on the extraction side for I3's MSI build).
